checks_run: Manual contract, implementation, test, documentation, and progressive-disclosure review
Pinned Node.js version check and syntax check of all submitted .mjs files
Independent aggregate and direct replay of sealed reference and adversarial tests
Independent 514-execution semantic/operator oracle matrix across tree and VM backends
Input non-mutation and malformed-bytecode boundary probes

evidence: The configured /arm/tools/nodejs/node/22.21.0/linux64/bin/node reported v22.21.0; all submitted JavaScript modules passed node --check.
The sealed suite passed as two file suites; direct execution passed 13/13 reference tests and 6/6 adversarial tests.
An independent direct-oracle matrix completed 514 tree/VM executions covering 250 numeric operator pairs and seven semantic programs with no mismatch.

Independent boundary probes confirmed no input mutation and controlled E_INVALID_BYTECODE rejection for accessor-backed, inherited, sparse-array, and malformed-span inputs; the tested getter was not invoked.
The public starter baseline exited 1 with lexer.test.mjs passing and parser.test.mjs plus execution.test.mjs failing, exactly as the candidate discloses for its TODO starter.

The pack audit reported PASS with 23 required files, 57 scanned files, zero forbidden paths, zero symlinks/special files, and zero credential-pattern matches; metadata identifiers and GENERATED/PARTIAL labels were internally consistent.
Reference CLI tree and VM stdin smoke runs both exited 0 and printed 8; the builder's material validation claims replayed without contradiction.
README.md advertises examples.mica, but no such file exists; the exact documented tree command exited 1 with ENOENT.

Sealed references, hidden-side tests, and exercise answers are readable in the same submitted tree, while the candidate supplies only naming/prose conventions and no independently verifiable learner-view projection.

REQUIREMENTS.md calls source Unicode but does not define whether offset/column count UTF-16 code units, code points, or graphemes; the supplied lexer uses UTF-16 units (PRINT after an emoji began at offset 6, column 7).
License and provenance prose clearly separates CC0 catalog metadata from the NOASSERTION linked resource and makes no production, fuzzing, benchmark, transfer, or stronger validation claim.
limitations: No orchestrator-produced learner view was supplied, so actual exclusion of every sealed path is inconclusive; if the harness already enforces and validates that projection, the disclosure finding is satisfied externally.

The immutable upstream baseline and linked repository were not available and network access was restricted, so source hashes, license evidence, and the no-copy claim could not be independently compared with upstream material.
Execution was limited to the pinned Node.js v22.21.0 runtime; no cross-runtime or cross-platform compatibility matrix was run.
The bounded example, matrix, and adversarial checks are not fuzzing, formal verification, a security certification, benchmarking, transfer verification, or production-readiness evidence.
The submitted starter is intentionally incomplete, so no completed learner implementation was available for acceptance testing.
rg and git were unavailable on PATH; bounded find and grep inspection was used instead, and neither missing utility blocked the JavaScript checks.
